videos.title: Breath that actually supports the phrase
videos.description: Low breath, soft ribs, and releasing on the vowel — not a big gasp before every line.

notes.abstract: Support comes from steady breath management, not forcing volume from the throat.
points: Inhale quietly into the lower ribs without lifting the shoulders.
Start the tone on the breath, not by squeezing the neck.
Practice on easy vowels before adding text.
notes.conclusion: If the sound thins at the end of a phrase, you ran out of managed air — shorten the phrase and rebuild.

videos.title: Finding pitch without chasing it
videos.description: Hum, slide, and land — a calm way to match pitch before you sing words.

notes.abstract: Pitch matching works better as a slide-and-land skill than as panic corrections mid-note.
points: Hum the target first, then open to a vowel.
Use sirens to feel the path between notes.
Record yourself and check against a reference tone.
notes.conclusion: Chasing pitch with the jaw usually makes it worse — quiet the body and listen first.

videos.title: Standing so the voice can move
videos.description: Balanced posture for singing: unlocked knees, easy neck, and space for the ribs.

notes.abstract: Posture for singing is buoyant alignment, not rigid military stance.
points: Soft knees and a long neck beat locked legs.
Let the sternum float without flaring the ribs hard.
Check that the jaw can hang free while you stand tall.
notes.conclusion: If breath feels stuck, check the knees and jaw before blaming the lungs.

videos.title: Resonance that feels forward
videos.description: Mask placement cues without nasality — feeling vibration where the tone can ring.

notes.abstract: Forward resonance is a sensation of ring, not pushing sound into the nose.
points: Start with NG–AH slides to feel the mask.
Keep the soft palate responsive, not clamped.
If it turns nasal, widen the vowel slightly and reduce squeeze.
notes.conclusion: Ring with ease beats brightness with tension.

videos.title: Audition day checklist
videos.description: What to warm, what to skip, and how to pace energy before you walk in.

notes.abstract: Auditions are won in the warm-up plan and the first 20 seconds of presence.
points: Warm enough to feel free, not enough to fatigue.
Decide tempo and opening intention before you enter.
Leave one easy phrase in reserve for nerves.
notes.conclusion: Over-warming is a common audition leak — stop while you still feel fresh.

resorts.name: Daily 12-minute warm-up
resorts.summary: A short sequence you can repeat before repertoire.
resorts.intro:
Use this as a default warm-up when you have little time.

1) Easy sirens
2) Lip trills on five-note patterns
3) One comfortable song phrase at half voice

Stop if the throat feels scratchy — switch to hums and hydration.

resorts.name: Voice care week
resorts.summary: Hydration, rest, and when to stop singing.
resorts.intro:
Voice care is boring until you need it.

Hydrate early in the day, not only mid-rehearsal. Sleep beats another late run-through when the voice is tired.

Pain, persistent hoarseness, or sudden range loss means rest and, if needed, a professional — not more pushing.
